newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ PLAYERS ACCUSED OF LATE NIGHT FROLICS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ PLAYERS ACCUSED OF LATE NIGHT FROLICS.

text.p: New Zealand Cricket (NZC) on Sunday sought to limit damage over allegations that several players were seen drinking in Wellington bars in the early of the morning during the second test against England.
New Zealand's weekly Sunday News claimed that allrounder Chris Cairns returned to the New Zealand team's hotel about 4 a.m. on Saturday morning.
Four other New Zealand players were also reported to have been seen drinking in bars in the city about 1.30 a.m.
At that stage of the game, England were 204 for three in reply to New Zealand's disastrous first innings 124.
Cairns played no part in the test on Saturday after bruising a finger the previous day.
NZC chief executive Christopher Doig angrily refused to comment on the issue after team manager and former All Blacks captain John Graham denied any wrongdoing by his players in a written statement.
Doig said four New Zealand players went out for a meal on Friday night.
"Three returned at 12.15 a.m. which the team management found acceptable," Doig said.
"One player was later than that. He has been spoken to by the team manager (Graham) and (Graham) pointed out that his time of return to the hotel was unacceptable.
"The matter is being dealt with internally. As far as we (NZC) are concerned that is the end of the matter."

Doig refused to identify the players involved and did not say what time the late player finally returned to the team hotel. He also refused to say what, if any, punishment had been meted out to that player.
"That'll remain within the team. I can't tell you because I don't know and don't need to know," Doig said.
"I am satisfied from the team manager that it has been appropriately dealt with," he said.
A Wellington taxi driver rang a local radio station on Saturday morning to say he had dropped Cairns off at the Plaza International Hotel in Wellington about 4 a.m.

Graham said the allegations that players were out in the early hours of Saturday morning "are not accurate and the New Zealand team management is satisfied that all players were fully prepared and focused on the task at hand today".
The allegations add to a bad record of off-field behaviour by players in the New Zealand team including an incident in 1995 when three players were suspended for smoking cannabis.
Team management also denied charges of ball tampering against New Zealand fast bowler Geoff Allott during Saturday's play in the second test.
